title: Lists
description: Store many values in order inside a single variable using a list.

content.value: So far, a variable held one value at a time. A list lets you store many values in one variable, kept in order. Think of it like a numbered row of slots, each holding one item.
You make a list by putting the items inside square brackets `[ ]`, separated by commas.
To get one item, you use its position number, called its index. Important: Python starts counting at 0. So index 0 is the first item, index 1 is the second, and so on.

toys = ["Lego", "Teddy Bear", "Action Figure"]
print(toys[0])  # Prints Lego
print(toys[2])  # Prints Action Figure
To add a new item to the end of a list, use `.append()`.

toys = ["Lego", "Teddy Bear"]
toys.append("Water Gun")
print(toys)  # Prints: ['Lego', 'Teddy Bear', 'Water Gun']

quiz.question: What index does the first item in a list have?
quiz.explain: Python counts from 0, so the first item is at index 0, the second at index 1, and so on.

quiz.question: Which method adds an item to the end of a list?
quiz.explain: `append()` adds an item to the end of a list. `insert()` adds at a chosen position, and `add()` isn't a list method.
